description: Names, MIME types and sizes attached to files a user chose. All three are attacker-influenced: the name comes from the file system, and `File.type` is a browser guess from the extension and the OS registry rather than a measurement of the bytes. The `file` sink asks whether the control's own limits held on the path they are actually enforced on; the `text` and `attribute` sinks ask whether the name is rendered as data once it is in the list.

fixtures.title: executable dropped into an image-only control
fixtures.rationale: `accept` on `<input type="file">` filters the operating system's picker and does nothing at all to `DataTransfer.files`, so the drop path is where a control's stated limit either exists or does not. `rejected` means the file never enters the model and an error is emitted — not that the upload is secure, which only a server can decide.
fixtures.provenance: HTML Standard: `accept` is a picker hint. Finding F1 in DzFileUpload.threat-model.md.

fixtures.title: double extension whose real type is not accepted
fixtures.rationale: Only the last extension is the extension. A check that searches the name for an accepted suffix anywhere, rather than matching the end of it, admits this.
fixtures.provenance: Standard double-extension case; OWASP file-upload guidance.

fixtures.title: file the browser could not type, against a MIME-only accept
fixtures.rationale: `File.type` is frequently the empty string. With no extension to fall back on and an `accept` that names only MIME types, the conservative answer is refusal. The opposite choice — admitting anything untyped — turns the whole control into a decoration.

fixtures.title: file name that is an img element with a handler
fixtures.rationale: A file name is host-supplied content that reaches at least two escaping contexts — the visible row and the remove control's accessible name — and getting one right says nothing about the other. Asserted against the DOM: no element created, no `on*` attribute on anything.
fixtures.provenance: cure53 markup case, applied to the file-name source.

fixtures.title: file name shaped to break out of an attribute value
fixtures.rationale: The name lands in an `aria-label`, which is attribute context. The decoy `x=` is retained from the markup file for the same reason: a pass that comes from an `on*`-only filter is not a pass.
fixtures.provenance: OWASP filter-evasion cheat sheet, attribute-context section.

fixtures.title: file name containing a relative path
fixtures.rationale: `File.name` is specified to hold no path, but a component must not be the reason a host believes that: the value is displayed and forwarded, and the outcome the component owes is that it is rendered as data. Whether the server joins it onto a directory is the server's finding, and this fixture is the one to point at when writing that up.
fixtures.provenance: File API `File.name` (no path); OWASP path-traversal guidance.

fixtures.title: 4 096-character file name
fixtures.rationale: The oversized case on the file-name source specifically, because a file list is a flow container and a name that does not wrap pushes the remove control off the row it belongs to. Same containment property as the degenerate-input file, asserted where it is reachable through a real API.
fixtures.provenance: Filesystem name-length limits; the length the existing DzFileUpload corpus already used.
